Kupiskis Jewish Cemetery 1

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the older of two numbered Jewish cemeteries in Kupiškis — known in Yiddish as Kupishok — whose Jewish community traces to 1682, when the local nobleman Pacas granted rights to build a synagogue. The community split formally into Hasidic and Mitnagdim factions, maintaining two rabbis, two ritual slaughterers, and three synagogues between them, and peaked at 2,661 people (71 percent of the town) in the late 19th century, before significant emigration — first to the United States, and for some, later on to South Africa — reduced its numbers. This older cemetery, likely established in the second half of the 17th century, remained untouched even after a newer cemetery took over burials in the 19th century, but was mostly destroyed during the Soviet era, when residential houses were built on its grounds; it was included in Lithuania's Register of Cultural Heritage after independence was restored in 1993. The record contains a contradiction: it is classified as not demolished, yet its own preservation-condition category states it was demolished and not built over — flagged here rather than resolved, especially given local testimony that houses were in fact built on the site.
